questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.topic: Biotechnology: Telling an Edited Allele From the Original on a Gel
questions.learningObjective: assign a genotype from band positions in a genotyping reaction

stimulus.body: Laboratory note (written for this course): A genotyping reaction amplifies across a site into which a 1,200 base pair sequence has been inserted in some individuals. The same pair of primers is used on every sample and in every lane, and an unedited individual gives a single product of 3,000 base pairs. A ladder of known lengths is run in the same gel. Lane one gives bands at 3,000 and 4,200 base pairs, lane two gives a single band at 3,000, and lane three gives a single band at 4,200.

questions.stem: Using only the laboratory note, what does each lane show?

options.text: Lane one has both alleles, lane two is unedited, and lane three carries the insertion on both copies
Lane one has both alleles, lane two is unedited, and lane three carries the insertion on one copy only
options.misconception: calls a single 4,200 band heterozygous, which requires both sizes to be present

options.text: Lane one is unedited, lane two carries the insertion on one copy, and lane three on both copies
options.misconception: mislabels which lane shows the unedited and which the edited genotype

options.text: Lane one has an unrelated deletion, lane two is unedited, and lane three carries a larger allele
options.misconception: reads an insertion as a deletion, so the larger band cannot be explained

questions.explanation: The 1,200 base pair insertion makes the amplified region 3,000 plus 1,200, which is 4,200 base pairs, and a 4,200 band therefore reports an allele carrying the insertion. An individual with one copy of each allele has both templates in the same cell, so the reaction makes both products and lane one shows a 3,000 band and a 4,200 band, which is the heterozygous pattern. A single 3,000 band in lane two means both copies are unedited, and a single 4,200 band in lane three means both copies carry the insertion, which is the homozygous edited case. The reason a single band can be read as homozygous rather than as a failed reaction is the presence of a control showing the reaction works at all, and that is the weakness of the design as given: a lane that amplified nothing would also show no band. Adding a second primer pair of known size to every lane would close that gap. Note also that the larger product migrates more slowly, so the 4,200 band is the upper one and the 3,000 band the lower. The tempting belief that lane three is heterozygous fails because a heterozygote must show both sizes. The belief that lane one is unedited fails because the extra band is there. The belief that the 4,200 band is a deletion fails because the insert makes the region longer, not shorter.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.topic: Biotechnology: Establishing That an Enzyme Drives an Industrial Step
questions.learningObjective: design a comparison that separates an enzyme's contribution from heating's
questions.stem: An enzyme is claimed to convert a starch slurry to sugar during a process that also heats the slurry. Describe an experiment that would show how much of the conversion the enzyme is responsible for.

answer.exemplar: Run the same slurry at the same temperature through four vessels, differing only in the enzyme: one with the enzyme, one with a boiled preparation of the same enzyme that has been denatured, one with an enzyme of unrelated activity added in the same amount, and one with no addition at all. Sampling at intervals rather than only at the end gives the rate as well as the total, and it is the rate that shows the enzyme is working on the substrate rather than the measurement drifting. The extension worth adding is to vary the enzyme amount across a series: if the rate rises with the amount at first and then levels off, the enzyme is genuinely limiting the step and adding more of it is a real design option, whereas a flat response means something else is the constraint. The constants that matter are the temperature, which must be identical in all four vessels, the amount of slurry, the sampling times, and the assay used to measure sugar, since a chemical test specific for the product is needed to distinguish conversion from the liquefaction the heating alone produces.

questions.explanation: The design needs a denatured-enzyme arm and an unrelated-enzyme arm as well as a no-enzyme arm, because the process also heats the slurry, and without the first two the change in the product cannot be separated from the effect of adding any protein at all.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.topic: Biotechnology: Testing an Antibody's Specificity and Its Usefulness
questions.learningObjective: design a panel that separates specific binding from non-specific sticking
questions.stem: A new antibody is claimed to bind one protein and nothing else. Describe an experiment that would test both halves of the claim, and say what a good candidate looks like on it.

answer.exemplar: Test a panel rather than a single pair, because specificity is a statement about everything the antibody fails to bind as much as about what it binds. Put the target on one spot and on the same panel put a set of unrelated proteins, a protein from the same organism but a different family, the same protein from a related organism, and a well that receives buffer only. A strong signal on the target, none on the buffer and none on the unrelated proteins, together with a retained signal on the same protein from a related organism, is the pattern that matters: the first two say it is not just sticking to the surface, the third says it is specific at the family level, and the fourth is the evidence that makes the antibody useful, since the point of the assay is to recognise the protein across individuals. Vary the amount of protein on the plate, because an antibody that gives a signal at every concentration has arrived non-specifically. An unrelated antibody of the same class on a parallel plate is the control that shows the low background belongs to the assay rather than to the target, and washing harder and re-reading the plate is what separates weak specific binding from strong non-specific sticking, since specific binding survives a stringent wash and sticking does not. Holding the coating amount, the blocking, the incubation time and the temperature identical across the panel is what makes one signal comparable with another.

questions.explanation: The panel has to include a buffer-only well, unrelated proteins and a related organism's version of the same protein, because the first two rule out non-specific binding and the third is what shows the antibody is specific enough to be worth using rather than merely specific to one sample.
questions.hint: Ask what the antibody must fail to bind for the specificity claim to mean anything, and what would make it useful.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.topic: Immunology: Testing Whether a Vaccine Induces the Intended Response
questions.learningObjective: design an outcome test tied to the vaccine's stated mechanism
questions.stem: A vaccine is claimed to protect people against a disease caused by an organism. Describe an experiment that would test whether that claim is true, and name one thing such a test can and cannot establish.

answer.exemplar: The test is a controlled exposure or a field trial with two arms: a group given the vaccine and a matched group given an inert injection, with the people in the two arms drawn from the same population, followed the same way, and assessed without knowledge of which arm they are in. Then count disease in each arm and compare, and the reason a matched control is indispensable is that disease also varies with season, with exposure, and with who happens to be in the group, so a single arm has nothing to be compared against. Measuring the immune response as well is what ties the outcome to the mechanism, since a vaccine that produces the intended response and no reduction in disease tells you the response is not the protective thing, which is a result worth having. What such a trial can establish is whether the vaccine reduces disease under the conditions of the trial, and how large that reduction is. What it cannot establish is that it will do so in a different population, against a different strain, or for as long as the trial lasted, because a trial is necessarily short, is run in a particular setting, and can only follow people for a limited time, so the size of the protection after a year and the effect in a population unlike the one studied remain open questions. The constants are the eligibility criteria, the dose schedule, the definition of a case, the follow-up length and the criteria by which a case is counted, all of which have to be fixed before the trial starts rather than chosen afterwards.

questions.explanation: The design needs a matched control arm, blinding and a pre-fixed case definition, and the explanation has to separate what a trial can show about its own setting from what it leaves open for other populations, longer times and other strains.

questions.learningObjective: convert an observed difference between two sequences into an elapsed time

The halving is the whole correction, and it is the reason two species that are half as different are not twice as old. questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.topic: Bioinformatics: Why a Shape Is Not a Function
questions.learningObjective: explain what a predicted structure supports and what it does not
questions.stem: A protein of unknown function is modelled, and the model returns a confident shape with a deep pocket lined by a few unusual residues. Explain what that picture supports, and why it is not yet evidence of a function.

answer.exemplar: A predicted structure is a hypothesis about shape, and a deep pocket lined by unusual residues is the kind of feature that genuinely suggests a binding partner, because a cavity is a place something can sit and the residues lining it are the ones that would make the contacts. So the picture is worth acting on, and it is the right kind of thing to publish a hypothesis about. What it does not do is establish a function, for three separate reasons. The method is fitted to sequences whose fold is determined by their sequence, so a protein whose shape depends on a partner, a metal ion, a membrane or a partner molecule in the cell is being modelled without the thing that determines its shape, and a confident-looking answer is still an answer to the wrong question. The unusual residues in the pocket may be wrong for the same reason, since they are inferred rather than observed, and a pocket built of misjudged residues is a pocket that is not there. Most importantly, a fold is used by many different proteins, so the same shape can occur in a protein that binds a small molecule, one that binds a protein and one that catalyses nothing at all, and shape alone does not choose between them. The picture therefore identifies what to test, and a test means finding a partner, a change or a catalytic activity and seeing whether it depends on that pocket, which is the step that turns a structural hypothesis into a functional claim. The habit worth forming is to state the model limits alongside the model, since a prediction of a flexible region, a multi-chain assembly or a protein with no known relatives is not a weaker version of the same answer but a different kind of answer.

questions.explanation: The explanation has to separate what the picture supports, which is a testable guess about a binding site, from what would be needed to call it a function, and it has to name the fold-sharing and missing-partner limits rather than only saying the model may be wrong.
questions.hint: Ask what the model was not given that the real protein would have had, and how many proteins can share one fold.

questions.topic: Bioethics: Why Consent Cannot Be Taken From Future People
questions.learningObjective: explain the consent and reversibility problems posed by a heritable change
questions.stem: A change is proposed in a fertilised egg so that it would be inherited by every descendant of the person born from it. Explain why the people affected by it cannot be asked, and what follows from the answer.

answer.exemplar: The people affected are not born yet, and that is the whole of the consent problem rather than a technicality attached to it. Consent is an agreement between a person and a decision that affects that person, and a person who does not exist cannot give one, cannot be consulted about how much risk is acceptable, and cannot decline. Nor can anyone else be asked on their behalf, because a parent's agreement covers the parent's own interests and the parent's genes, not the separate interests of a descendant a hundred years out, who may or may not want the change. What follows is that the burden of proof runs in an unusual direction, because the party who would object most is the one with no voice in the decision, so the case for proceeding has to be made without the benefit of the objection and the case against is made by the mere existence of the asymmetry. Two further features compound it. The change is not reversible in the people who carry it, because it is in every cell including the germ cells, so a mistake cannot be withdrawn from a descendant the way a treatment can be stopped in a patient. And its later effects are not fully predictable from its immediate ones, since a change intended to remove a disease may have consequences for a life that has never been lived, and nobody is in a position to describe those consequences in advance. This is why the argument is not that the intervention is always wrong, since treating a single person with a body-cell change is a different case with a different structure, but that a heritable intervention requires a stronger justification than the same intervention confined to one consenting person, and that the people who would have to live with the consequences of a wrong decision cannot be asked whether they accept them.

questions.explanation: The explanation has to locate the problem in consent and reversibility for people who do not yet exist, and then draw the consequence that a heritable intervention faces a higher burden of justification than the same change confined to a consenting individual, rather than resting the argument on a prediction of whether the change is good.
questions.hint: Ask who would have to consent to a change they will only discover they carry, and whether anyone can withdraw it for them.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.topic: Biotechnology: Ordering the Route From Immunisation to a Cell Line
questions.learningObjective: order the steps that turn an immune response into a single antibody source
questions.stem: The five steps below run from the first exposure of an animal to a purified antibody. Put them in the order in which they are carried out.

options.text: An animal is exposed to the target so that many different antibodies are produced
Cells making the wanted antibody are taken from the animal and fused with dividing cells
The fused cells are separated from those that did not fuse, and grown as clones
Each clone is tested to find which ones make the antibody wanted
A chosen clone is grown in quantity and its antibody is purified from the culture

questions.explanation: The order follows from the fact that the wanted cell has to exist before it can be kept alive and multiplied. Exposure comes first because until the animal has made an immune response there are no cells making any particular antibody to take, and the exposure deliberately produces many different ones so that a wanted specificity is somewhere in the mixture. The fusion then supplies the one property the animal's own cells lack, which is the ability to divide indefinitely, so the two halves of the resulting cell are the specificity from one cell and the growth from the other. Separation comes next because the fusion is inefficient and most cells are unjoined, so the mixture has to be reduced to the fused cells before anything can be attributed to them, and it is done by a selection that kills the cells lacking the fused cell's combined properties. Testing the clones comes after the separation because a test needs a clone to test and a clone means a single lineage, and the point of testing is that fusion is random and the wanted antibody is not what any particular fusion happened to produce. Growing and purifying comes last because there is nothing worth growing in quantity until one clone has been shown to make the antibody wanted. The wrong order that tests before separating fails because a mixed culture gives a result attributable to none of its cells. The wrong order that grows before testing fails because the culture would be a mixture of many specificities.
questions.hint: Ask which step has to happen before there is a single cell to attribute a result to.

questions.subject: BIOLOGY
questions.topic: Biotechnology: Ordering the Route From a Guide to a Confirmed Edit
questions.learningObjective: order the stages that produce and then verify a targeted sequence change
questions.stem: These five stages take a chosen site in a molecule from its first design to a confirmed cell line. Put them in the order they happen.

options.text: A short guide sequence is chosen to match the chosen place in the target molecule
The guide and the nuclease are delivered into the cell, and the nuclease cuts both strands there
The cell's own repair closes the break, using the supplied donor sequence as its template
Individual cells are examined to find one in which the intended change is present
The change is confirmed by an independent method and the resulting line is kept

questions.explanation: The order is a chain of dependencies, and the last two steps are the ones most often skipped. The guide has to be chosen first because it is what directs the nuclease, and choosing it is a design step that fails silently if the target is not unique, since a guide that also matches elsewhere will cut elsewhere. The cut then has to happen before the repair, because the break is the opportunity and the donor sequence has nothing to be used at until the cell has been made to copy it. The repair is the cell's, which is why the change is not fully specified in advance and why examining individual cells is necessary rather than optional, because the same delivery can give a clean edit, an edit in the wrong place, a re-closed molecule and a large deletion, and only looking distinguishes them. Confirmation comes last and by an independent method, because a screen using the same machinery that made the change can be fooled by it, so a separate measurement of the sequence is what turns a candidate into a confirmed line. The tempting order that cuts before the guide is chosen fails because there is nothing to direct the cut. The order that inserts the donor before the break fails because there is no break to repair. The order that keeps the line before confirming it fails because an unconfirmed cell may carry any of the several outcomes rather than the intended one.
questions.hint: Ask what each step needs to have already happened, and which step exists to catch a wrong outcome.
